text:
About the Initiative

Monthly · Bayes Business School

Research seminars for the PhD community
FAM PhD Talks brings together PhD students and faculty members across research areas for regular research presentations and discussion. The series provides a space for doctoral researchers to present work in progress, receive feedback, and engage with methodological and conceptual questions beyond their immediate research group.
As co-founder and organiser, I help coordinate the series, including speaker planning, scheduling, event communication, and the development of a regular forum for PhD research exchange.

title: Research
text:
Publications & Working Papers
My research lies at the intersection of actuarial science, mathematical finance, and sustainable investment. I develop continuous-time stochastic control models to study how individuals, pension funds, and firms make long-term financial decisions under uncertainty, with a focus on financial risk, labour income, longevity risk, pension design, and sustainability-related constraints.

title: Research
text:
Revise-and-Resubmit


Journal: Quantitative Finance


The Sustainability Trade-Off: A Dynamic Constrained Portfolio Optimization Model with ESG Preferences

with Andrea Buffoli and Francesco Menoncin

This paper studies the trade-off faced by investors who care about both financial performance and sustainability. We model ESG preferences as constraints on portfolio composition in a continuous-time investment problem, showing how these constraints change the investor’s attainable wealth and optimal strategy. The framework provides closed-form solutions and measures the cost of sustainability as the utility loss relative to an unconstrained Merton benchmark. We also study how subjective ESG beliefs affect perceived returns, portfolio allocation, and the set of attainable investment outcomes.

title: Research
text:
Work in Progress Papers

Optimal Sustainable Retirement Investing: Continuous-Time Portfolio Choice for Individual Retirement Plans with ESG Preferences

with Steven Haberman and Iqbal Owadally

This paper studies sustainable portfolio choice in an individual retirement plan during the accumulation phase. We develop a continuous-time model in which contributions are linked to labour income and investors balance terminal retirement wealth against a penalty for falling short of a chosen ESG benchmark. The optimal portfolio decomposes into the standard Merton allocation and an ESG adjustment, making the trade-off between financial performance and sustainability explicit and quantifiable.

Draft available upon request.



Endogenous Pension Accumulation in a Life-Cycle Model with Labor-Linked Contributions

with Andrea Buffoli

This paper studies how labour-market inequality accumulates over the life cycle and translates into pension inequality at retirement. We develop a continuous-time life-cycle model in which individuals jointly choose consumption, labour supply, portfolio allocation, and retirement timing while facing stochastic wages, financial market risk, mortality risk, and pension accumulation. The framework embeds gender-specific labour-market profiles to study how wages, working hours, career interruptions, portfolio choices, and survival prospects affect retirement incentives and pension adequacy.

title: Research
text:
Research Agenda

My research agenda is organised around three connected themes. First, I study long-term household and pension decisions, focusing on how labour income, longevity risk, pension rules, and retirement incentives shape consumption, labour supply, portfolio choice, pension accumulation, and retirement timing.


Second, I study sustainable investment in dynamic settings. This work examines how ESG preferences shape optimal portfolio choice in retirement and investment problems, and how sustainability objectives interact with financial performance, risk, and long-term wealth outcomes.


Third, I examine sustainability-related risks at the firm level, including greenwashing risk and the gap between perceived and substantive sustainability. This strand studies how verification risk, information-driven repricing, and reputational incentives affect investment, payout, leverage, and sustainability effort.


Methodologically, my work combines stochastic control, optimal stopping, dynamic portfolio choice, and numerical analysis. My aim is to develop models that are mathematically rigorous, tractable, and closely connected to questions in actuarial science, pension finance, and sustainable finance.

title: Teaching
text:
Instruction & Mentoring
I have taught and supported students in finance, quantitative methods, VBA, financial mathematics, and one-to-one tutorials. My teaching interests include actuarial science, financial economics, portfolio theory, risk management, optimisation, applied statistics, and quantitative finance.

title: Teaching
text:
Teaching Experience

MA2614 Financial and Investment Mathematics B

Bayes Business School · City St George’s, University of London

This module builds on the foundations of Financial and Investment Mathematics A. It applies compound-interest theory and present- and future-value methods to the analysis and valuation of financial cash flows and investment products. The module also examines the interaction between interest rates and financial markets, the sensitivity of portfolios to changes in interest rates, and the use of stochastic interest-rate models in financial valuation.


MA1614 Financial and Investment Mathematics A

Bayes Business School · City St George’s, University of London

This module introduces the foundations of financial mathematics and their application to simple investment problems. It develops the core mathematical tools needed to quantify the time value of money and provides students with a rigorous basis for analysing financial cash flows and investment decisions.
